newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo sees 2000 sales at 10 trln won.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo sees 2000 sales at 10 trln won.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Electronics Co Ltd, a unit of the Daewoo Group, said on Friday it had revised its sales forecast for the year 2000 to 10 trillion won from a previous prediction of eight trillion won.
In 1995, the company reported a net profit of 47.23 billion won on sales of 2.13 trillion.
In a statement, the company said it had raised its expectations following sharply rising export sales and plans to expand its overseas production capacity.
As part of this plan, Daewoo said it would start increasing production at overseas plants this year.
Annual production from a colour television plant in Mexico will be boosted to three million units by the end of the year from two million currently, it said.
Annual production of microwave ovens at a factory in France will be expanded to two million from 1.5 million currently, while the plant's colour television output will rise to 800,000 from 600,000.
A plant in Poland will see its 400,000-unit colour television production capacity double to 800,000 units, and its printed circuit board lines will be boosted to 10 from the current three.
A British video cassette recorder factory will see its annual capacity increased to one million units from 800,000.
Daewoo said overseas demand for its consumer electronics products was almost twice domestic demand, and it expected to see 1996 exports 50 percent higher than last year's.
Daewoo plans to invest $500 million by the year 2000 on overseas investments, a company spokesman said.
